explanation: Free-fall body 0 gains ~2.3 m/s in a single dt=0.0265 step under g=14.45 (expected g*dt~0.38). Step reports 46/43 substeps triggered by fast body 1, indicating gravity impulse is applied per-substep with full-step magnitude, multiplying free-fall acceleration by substep count. This injects hundreds of J with controller_work=0 and no contacts, breaching energy_bound at step 2. Small-dt counterfactual removes substep amplification and conserves energy.
vision_note: The lower body falls to the floor between step 0 and step 1 and is airborne again by step 2, covering an anomalously large distance in just two steps. The upper body barely moves, highlighting the excessively fast drop and rebound of the lower body.
